title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: Hold: the licensing paragraph omits a documented entitlement and could lead administrators to buy unnecessary licences. Microsoft now also lists Dynamics licences that include Power Apps use rights as an option for running code apps; the briefing's other commands, control paths and roadmap facts are supported.

claims.claim: This Power Apps change is roadmap item 576782 about CLI connector discovery and connection creation for code apps.
claims.quote: "id": 576782; "title": "PowerApps: Building modern apps - Use CLI to discover, create, and wire connectors in code apps"; "products": ["Power Apps"]

claims.claim: The CLI adds commands for developers to discover available connectors.
claims.quote: The Power Apps CLI adds new commands that let developers discover available connectors and create connections directly from the command line.

claims.claim: The CLI adds commands for developers to create connections from the command line.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The feature settings page lists Enable code apps with a default of Off.
claims.quote: | Enable code apps | Allow users to bring apps they created outside of Power Apps and run them in Power Apps.  If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run.Learn more about Power Apps code apps. | Off |

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: first paragraph
claims.claim: Code apps do not run when Enable code apps is turned off.
claims.quote: If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run.

claims.claim: Power Platform admins and environment admins can set the environment option for code apps.
claims.quote: Admins can enable code apps by setting an environment option. Power Platform admins and environment admins can set this option.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment groups and rules can configure the code apps setting for multiple environments.
claims.quote: For management at scale, you can configure this setting for multiple environments at once by using environment groups and rules.

claims.claim: The environment toggle is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Power Apps code apps > Enable code apps.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments > select the environment where you use code apps.
Go to Settings > Expand the Product subsection > Select Features.
Go to the feature Power Apps code apps and use the Enable code apps toggle to turn it on.

claims.claim: A runnable operation documented to set the environment's Enable code apps control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerAppsAllowCodeApps update environment PowerShell API; Enable code apps API PowerShell pac admin; PowerApps_AllowCodeApps PATCH. Opened SDK property, overview and Environment Management Settings update reference; no request property mapping for this toggle.

claims.claim: The .NET SDK exposes nullable Boolean PowerAppsAllowCodeApps on EnvironmentManagementSetting.
claims.quote: public bool? PowerAppsAllowCodeApps { get; set; }

claims.claim: The PowerAppsAllowCodeApps property reference itself does not give a runnable update operation.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerAppsAllowCodeApps update environment PowerShell API. Opened the complete EnvironmentManagementSetting.PowerAppsAllowCodeApps property reference; it gives the nullable Boolean definition and property value, but no update call.

claims.claim: A blockable connector can be blocked at Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Security in the navigation pane.
under Settings, select Data and privacy.
select the Data policy section.
select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
Select the Prebuilt connectors step
For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> sets connector classifications in a DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>
If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.claim: Classification values General, Confidential and Blocked correspond to Non-business, Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Each connector object supplied to Add-ConnectorsToPolicy requires id, type and name properties.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- id: The unique identifier of the connector.
- type: The type of the connector:
- name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.claim: The Block action is available only for blockable connectors.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Code apps have a mixed licensing model, including licensed and pay-as-you-go entitlement options.
claims.quote:
End users that run code apps need one of the following:
- Power Apps Premium license
- Pay-as-you-go enabled
- An App Pass
- Auto-claim enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: second paragraph
claims.claim: End users running code apps need Power Apps Premium, pay-as-you-go, an App Pass or auto-claim.
claims.quote:
End users that run code apps need one of the following:
- Power Apps Premium license
- Pay-as-you-go enabled
- An App Pass

claims.fix: In licensing.notes and the second Cost and licensing paragraph, add 'or Dynamics licences that include Power Apps use rights' to the list of qualifying entitlements. The overview now explicitly includes this fifth option: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/code-apps/overview#license-end-users-with-power-apps-premium.

claims.claim: A limit specific to this CLI connector-command feature is not published.
